issues.body: completeness() returns planned=None not only for legacy artifacts but also when mutants.json is missing, corrupt, unreadable, or the wrong shape, and seed() then accepts the outcomes without any completeness check. A timed-out artifact copied without mutants.json is therefore accepted as a whole run—the exact dishonest-baseline failure this change claims to prevent. The self-test explicitly requires this unsafe behavior for t3. This also contradicts the new ci.yml and baseline prose saying --seed refuses a truncated run; it only refuses one when valid sidecar evidence happens to be present.
issues.fix_hint: Fail closed in --seed when completeness cannot be established: record missing/invalid mutants.json as a seed refusal, while allowing --check to remain backward-compatible if desired. If a legacy escape hatch is necessary, make it explicit and loudly named, and update all claims accordingly. Replace the t3 acceptance assertion with missing, malformed, and wrong-shape sidecar refusal tests.
issues.title: Seeding still fails open when planned-mutant evidence is unavailable

issues.body: The new comments publish exact mutant counts, per-mutant seconds, runner-hours, means, and derived wall-clock ranges from a four-CPU/session box. The reviewer contract explicitly prohibits hard-coded performance numbers and says work-box/session-box timings are non-canonical. These figures will also stale as the crate and runner environment change, while appearing authoritative in the workflow.
issues.fix_hint: Remove the exact timing/count/range claims from the workflow. Keep a qualitative sizing rationale and point to a reproducible generated artifact or tracked measurement record if evidence is needed; describe the 24-way split as an operational initial value to be retuned from nightly results, without presenting local timings as canonical.
issues.title: Workflow hard-codes non-canonical work-box performance measurements

verdict.summary: Round 2 fixes the prior shard-set defect: seeding now validates identities, uniqueness, denominators, and completeness, with non-vacuous tests for the previously reported cases. However, truncation safety still fails open whenever mutants.json is absent, malformed, unreadable, or not a list; the self-test explicitly blesses that path even though the workflow comments and baseline documentation claim truncated runs are refused. The diff also embeds session-box timing/count measurements despite the repository rule that such figures are non-canonical and must not be hard-coded. Because these are new findings relative to round 1, progress is regressing under the required scale.
